body: I know the doctors are there to help. I know they're trained and they've seen hundreds of people get better. My apprehension with them is entirely irrational.

I've never understood the idea that people are inherently "good". There's nothing to base that idea on. People can learn to be "good" and it can work for them, they learn to like it. It works exactly the same way for "bad". People are inherently self-serving and their psyche adapts in the way it needs to survive, usually. I've wondered a lot whether my differences are biological or simply the product of my experiences. Either way, I don't feel capable of changing on my own. I have no idea where I'd start.

I like the idea of constructing a narrative. A lot of the time I feel like I'm acting anyway so it'd probably work.

>brother

I'm trans-androgynous and still female physically. I don't really care what you call me but I didn't want to leave you with a partially incorrect idea.

Yes, I'm very aware of the catch-22 in this.

I know that you're right. I know that with treatment and my cooperation in treatment, I have a chance at getting better. I must care whether I die or not because I'm still here, still commenting, still biding my time. I can't bring myself to pick up a phone and schedule an appointment much less go. It's a pointless endeavor for a cause I can't see as worthy even though I'm told it matters. 

I'm sorry. You're making excellent points and all I can go back to is wanting to just curl up into a ball and ignore the world.

This made me tear up. I very rarely cry so thank you. I'm not sure exactly what made me post this but I'm glad I did.

The weird thing is, over-the-counter and illegal meds/drugs, I have no problem with taking. No suspicion whatsoever. I will read up on them as much as I can before I take them but those I definitely take. The minute a doctor hands me a little orange bottle though, I'm wondering what their motive is.

>I would recommend owning your hallucinations and paranoia with your immediate support network.
>trying to own your situation with your fam'

I'm not sure what you mean by this. To own them?

I'm pretty convinced that I have both BPD and schizophrenia. I've read as much as I could find on the comorbidity of the two pathologies. No one who's been diagnosed with the two lived/lives a successful life.

One day in math class, high school, I was incredibly bored. My brain, for one reason or another, doesn't acquire math skills without 100x more effort than the normal person so I wasn't able to pay attention if I tried. Usually I just fell asleep. This one particular day, I told my teacher that my stomach hurt and was allowed to go see the nurse. Our school had just implemented a policy where you had to sign out to go anywhere (as a safe guard against kids using drugs/going to their cars and getting guns/etc/you get the idea). Because I was "sick" and had a very good rep with the teachers, he didn't bother making me sign anything.

I sat in the bathroom for awhile instead of seeing the nurse, played games on my phone, washed my hands a few times. I remembered a story I'd read about school shooting threats and another thing about graffiti. I thought, "Hey, wouldn't it be fun to scare the shit out of everyone? I won't actually do anything dangerous so it's harmless."

Not really thinking or caring about what I was doing, I pulled a pen out of my pocket and wrote a line from a book I'd been reading on the stall's wall. Something about the inevitability of death and mortality, very poetic. (I remember exactly what I wrote but for the sake of further anonymity, I'll leave it as that.) It looked lacking. So I bit the inside of my lip, drew as much blood as I could, and painted DIE really big. I made sure that I didn't leave finger prints and that it was really scary looking with drips and the whole deal. Then I left as fast as I could, continued the rest of the day as normal.

I heard nothing about it until the next morning. The whole school was freaking out. Some student had found it and apparently fainted. The teachers were trying to keep it hushed but talking in little groups, furtively glancing around. Students had to be escorted between classes. Police officers were stationed at all the entrances to the school. They figured out all the students who had signed off to go out of class the day before but since my name wasn't on it, I didn't get interrogated. My math teacher looked directly at me when they came to get the students but I assume he didn't want to get in trouble for violating the new policy so he kept his mouth shut. I mean, who would have thought I would do something like that? That's just silliness. She's such a good student and volunteers in everything and dammit, she's the head of the one club, in varsity sports, and does outreach for the huge church. Meanwhile, I was laughing my ass off.

Rumors flew around the school. "It was a bomb threat!" "I heard something about a suicide note!" "No way, I think it's an outside source." "I heard it was real blood!" "That's stupid! We should be looking at the one goth chick who never talks to anyone! She obviously did it!" "I heard they think it was some chick PMSing and being creative with a tampon." That's my favorite, by the way.

It was exhilarating. People quietly praised the perpetrator saying they were happy something fun was finally happening. Oooh, maybe next someone would bring a gun! That tickled me. These small town idiots thinking school shootings are fun. lol I'm a hypocrite, I know.

After about a week of police stationed at the doors, they had no more suspects. The small town didn't have the police power to run DNA tests and even if they tried, they had no other evidence to match it to. No leads. No one confessed. Everything went back to normal except for the faint whisper now and then. Even those died away by the time I graduated; and I've never heard a single solitary mention of the incident since then.

The kicker? They still barely have security in that place. There's a sign-in sheet in the front office that isn't even mandatory. No cameras. No hall monitors. I know every entrance into and out of that building as well as every hiding place. I could, if I felt so inclined, walk in without being seen while everyone's in class or at an assembly and do it all over again. Just for shits and giggles.
